notes: Pole-mounted cooperative bank sign in Ilobasco seen from below; overhead wires cross 'de R.L.' and 'Sucursal Ilobasco'. The L's in the last line are painted as capital-style glyphs ('SucursaL ILobasco'). A small sideways number on the box edge ('...793-286...') is not legible.

author: Ll1324

notes: Orange fast-food fascia (sunburst sign) on a red-orange wall, slightly tilted. Distractors: 'Combos Familiares' poster with prices, menu board and 'SALIDA' sign inside. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: PABLO NUÑEZ
attribution: Photo: PABLO NUÑEZ, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Salcoatitan,_El_Salvador_-_panoramio_(3).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Carved wooden bakery sign on a yellow-and-blue shopfront in Salcoatitán, at an angle; a hanging orange 'PANADERIA' street sign at right is a secondary sign. Partly in shadow of the eave. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

Distractor billboard 'ARMANDO PAZ ... ¿HAY ALGO QUE QUIERAS CAMBIAR?' at left; vehicles with plates are small and incidental.

lines.text: EL ALCALDE Y SU CONCEJO MUNICIPAL
SE ENORGULLECEN DE ENTREGAR EL PROYECTO:

notes: Small brass commemorative plaque on a blue plinth in Parque Rafael Campo, Sonsonate, with the cathedral and a bust behind. Only the header and project title are transcribed; the rest of the plaque (dedication text, donor families, mayor 'JOSE ROBERTO AQUINO RUIZ', two columns of council names, date) is too small to read reliably. Crest legend 'SONSONATE' and the national seal ring text are tiny.

author: Argoel2
attribution: Photo: Argoel2, CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Estacion_Quezaltepeque.jpg. License: http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/deed.en. Unmodified original.
notes: Weathered brown former railway station board (Estación Ferroviaria Quezaltepeque) with many brass letters missing: only ghost outlines remain for the F, the O of FERROVIARIA, the Q, the L, the P and the final E; the N of ESTACIÓN hangs loose (not counted). Lines give only the letters still attached, with gaps as spaces. A green building labelled 'MUSEO DE QUEZALTEPEQUE' at left is a secondary sign; a rail bogie stands in front.
